# Vignettes

Worked examples of dose-response analysis with drc. Each is generated from a Nim program in [`vignettes/`](../../vignettes), so every output and figure comes from a real run. Re-render them with `nimble vignettes`.

- **[Getting started: fitting a dose-response curve](getting_started.md)**: Fit a four-parameter logistic curve to a classic data set, read off the EC50 and other effective doses with confidence intervals, draw the curve with its uncertainty, and check the fit through its residuals.
- **[Choosing a model](model_choice.md)**: drc fits three members of one family: the 3PL, the 4PL and the 5PL. This vignette shows when to fix a plateau, when an asymmetric 5PL earns its extra parameter, how to compare candidate models (by AIC, by a lack-of-fit test and by their residuals), and how bounds keep plateaus possible.
- **[Confidence intervals](intervals.md)**: drc gives three kinds of interval for a parameter or an effective dose: Wald (delta-method) intervals, profile-likelihood intervals and bootstrap intervals. On a well-designed experiment they agree. On a partial curve they do not, and the differences say how much the data really pin down.
- **[Outliers and robust fitting](outliers.md)**: A few bad wells can drag a least-squares curve a long way. This vignette finds them in the residuals, then fits the curve robustly with Huber and Tukey losses, which downweight or reject large residuals automatically, and compares that with removing known-bad wells by hand.
- **[Several curves and relative potency](potency.md)**: Fit several dose-response curves at once, test whether they are parallel, and estimate how potent each test sample is relative to a reference standard, with delta-method, profile-likelihood and bootstrap intervals.
- **[Standard curves and inverse prediction](standard_curves.md)**: Fit an ELISA standard curve, read the concentrations of unknown samples off it with calibration intervals, check the standards' recovery, and map the concentrations over which the assay is precise enough to report.
- **[Fitting many curves: a compound screen](screening.md)**: Fit one curve per compound across a whole screen, decide which compounds are real hits from the fits' warnings and intervals, and rank them. The data are simulated, so the estimates can be checked against the truth.
